reason: The cited evidence shows that SRO exists in HEAs (E1) and that lattice distortion affects dislocation activity (E2), but none of the passages demonstrate that SRO is mechanically degraded under load, that its loss triggers a creep mechanism switch, or that initial SRO controls creep rates. The key causal premises are unsupported by the cited studies.
premises: SRO impedes dislocation nucleation and motion in HEAs
Loss of SRO reduces barriers to dislocation motion
SRO degradation causes a switch from diffusion-dominated to dislocation-mediated creep
Higher initial SRO delays plastic flow onset and lowers creep rate
